summary.name: Good housekeeping for error budgets (CRE Life Lessons part two)
summary.one_liner: A 2018 Google Cloud Platform blog article, part two of the CRE Life Lessons series, on how to respond when a service overspends its SRE error budget: fix root causes, account for platform failures, and decide when and how long to freeze releases.
use_cases: deciding what to do when a service overspends its error budget
prioritizing reliability work over feature work after outages
choosing between fixed-calendar and rolling error budget windows
handling outages caused by a cloud platform or dependency
setting up a release freeze policy with exceptions
summary.what_it_does: The article is a written guide, not a software tool. It explains that once error budget spend analysis identifies the main causes, teams should redirect development effort from features to fixing those causes, such as better QA, testing, rollout automation and monitoring. It discusses separating overspend caused by platform or dependency outages from overspend caused by the team's own releases. It describes the feature freeze as a last-resort measure and lists alternatives such as an agreed change in feature vs. reliability work, overprovisioning, and declaring a reliability incident. It compares fixed-interval and rolling-interval error budget calculation and recommends rolling windows, and it covers the long-term costs of freezes and a "silver bullet" override process.
notable: Compares fixed calendar-month and rolling 30-day error budget windows, with a worked example
Describes a 'silver bullet' process letting product management override a release freeze for critical features
Warns that long release freezes can cause a backlog of broken releases afterward
caveats: Written guidance from Google's CRE team; it describes practices rather than providing a product or tool
Notes that rolling error budget windows are hard to accumulate in many current monitoring tools
